newsitem.title: PERU: Peru asks Germany to end rebel's asylum - report.
newsitem.headline: Peru asks Germany to end rebel's asylum - report.

text.p: Peru's Foreign Ministry has asked Germany to cancel political asylum status granted to the international spokesman for the Marxist rebel group involved in the hostage crisis, a local newspaper reported on Sunday.

Peruvian authorities were concerned that Isaac Velazco was using his asylum status "to launch threats and false information against the Peruvian government," the pro-government Expreso paper said, citing an unnamed foreign ministry source.
Velazco, a Peruvian who was granted asylum in Germany in 1993, became a key figure in the hostage drama as the main mouthpiece of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).

During 18 weeks leading up to last Tuesday's explosive end to the hostage siege, Velazco gave news conferences in several European cities and issued regular statements on behalf of the 14 rebels inside the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.
Velazco has been asked to appear before police in Hamburg this week for the first time since he arrived in Germany, he told Reuters by telephone last week.

Velazco said he carried a blue German passport issued by the United Nations since he is a political exile from Peru. He also said Swiss authorities had banned a planned MRTA rally scheduled for May 1.
Crack Peruvian troops stormed the diplomatic mansion in Lima on April 22, freeing all but one of the 72 hostages and killing all 14 MRTA rebels.
Since the assault, Velazco has warned that the MRTA was preparing to launch reprisal attacks throughout Peru.
The Expreso report said if German authorities did not strip Velazco's asylum, Peru may seek his extradition.
